scoreRationale: A small coastal-edge hamlet and route waypoint without an independently visitable centre or visitor-service cluster. Elliot Beach and West Links facilities belong to Arbroath and are not transferred into this score.

heritage.dateRule: Construction or material-period dates only; never designation, listing or database dates.

linkStatus.AngusCoastPath: Browser-resolvable official PDF; command-line request receives the council anti-bot response

practicalAudit.see: The 1958 ROC post is heritage evidence on private land, not a published attraction. West Links Beach belongs to Arbroath.
practicalAudit.eat: No cafe, tearoom, bakery café, coffee-and-cake stop or light-lunch venue verified in the strict hamlet.
practicalAudit.picnic: West Links picnic grass is an Arbroath facility and is not borrowed.
practicalAudit.parking: The council describes Elliot Links access within the wider Arbroath common-good parkland, but no exact hamlet public-car-park contract with capacity, tariff or restrictions was verified.
practicalAudit.toilets: West Links seasonal and Changing Places toilets are Arbroath facilities; no Elliot-hamlet public toilet was verified.
practicalAudit.accessibility: No independent Elliot visitor facility publishes an accessibility contract.
practicalAudit.transport: Elliot is a coast-path waypoint and A92-edge hamlet rather than a service centre.

exclusions: West Links Beach and park facilities remain with Arbroath.
The private ROC monitoring post is not promoted as a public attraction.
The coast path contributes no points to the settlement-only score.
